 Republican state party chair resigns following party losses on election day
 WFYI Public Media | 
 By
 Benjamin Thorp 
 Published November 13, 2026 at 2:44 PM CST
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Photo courtesy of Mike Braun for Indiana Gov. Mike Braun, left, endorsed Lana Keesling, right, to serve as chair of the Indiana Republican Party. Keesling stepped down following a tough election night for Republicans. 
 Indiana’s Republican Party chair has stepped down.
 The move comes following an election night that saw Republican seats flip across the state, and the party lose two statewide offices.
 Those losses included the sixteen seats in the Indiana House. Former speaker of the House Todd Huston (R-Fishers) was among them.
 The aftermath of that night has left many Republicans asking what the party missed and where things went wrong - both at the state and national level .
 In a statement, Chair Lana Keesling said it had been an incredible honor to serve the party.
 “I wish the next chair and the entire Indiana Republican Party continued success,” she said. Keesling did not give any specific reasons for her resignation.
 She has only served in the role since 2025 .
 Vice Chair Jim Johnson will assume the role of interim chair until a new one is elected.
 Gov. Mike Braun thanked Keesling for her service and called the change in leadership a “golden opportunity to strengthen our party and address the kitchen table issues facing families.”
 Braun said he looked forward to working with the GOP State Central Committee to select a new party chair.
